title: Informal Conjecture (fractional treewidth-fragility of sublinear-separator classes)
statement_text: All classes with sublinear separators are fractionally treewidth-fragile.
context_text: In this paper, For an $n$-vertex graph, a balanced separator is a set $X$ of vertices such that each component of $G-X$ has at most $2n/3$ vertices; a class $\mathcal{G}$ has strongly sublinear separators if every subgraph with at most $n$ vertices of a graph of $\mathcal{G}$ has a balanced separator of size $O(n^{1-\beta})$ for some fixed $\beta>0$ (by Dvořák and Norin these are exactly the classes of polynomial expansion). A multiset $\mathcal{Z}$ of vertex subsets of $G$ is an $(s,\delta)$-generic cover if every set of at most $s$ vertices is contained in at least $\delta|\mathcal{Z}|$ members of $\mathcal{Z}$; its treewidth is the maximum treewidth of $G[Z]$, $Z\in\mathcal{Z}$. A class is fractionally treewidth-fragile if there is a function $f$ such that every $G$ in the class has, for all positive integers $s,o$, an $(s,1-1/o)$-generic cover of treewidth at most $f(os)$ (equivalently, in the usual formulation: there is a system of vertex sets, each vertex lying in at most a $1/o$ fraction of them, whose deletion each leaves treewidth at most $f(o)$); it is efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile if such a cover (of polynomial size) can be found in polynomial time. The author proves that, for every first-order expressible monotone maximization problem, efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile classes admit a PTAS. These classes include all hereditary classes with sublinear separators and bounded maximum degree, all proper minor-closed classes, and many geometric graph classes such as intersection graphs of convex sets with bounded aspect ratio and bounded clique number in a fixed Euclidean space. The author remarks that it is possible, and the author has conjectured, that the property extends to all classes with sublinear separators (the phrase is used here without the word 'strongly', the paper's general notion being strongly sublinear separators).
notes: Stated in running prose as 'it is possible (and I have conjectured) that all classes with sublinear separators are fractionally treewidth-fragile'.
paper_title: Approximation metatheorems for classes with bounded expansion

title: Problem 6
statement_text: Do monotone minimization problems expressible in the first order logic admit constant factor approximation in all classes with bounded expansion? And PTASes in all efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile graph classes?
context_text: For a finite index set $I$, a property $\pi$ of $I$-tuples $A_I=(A_i)_{i\in I}$ of vertex subsets of $G$ is expressible in first-order logic if it is the set of tuples satisfying a fixed first-order sentence using quantification over vertices, the adjacency predicate, equality and unary predicates $X_i$ interpreted as the sets $A_i$. Given a weight assignment $w(v,J)\ge0$ for each vertex $v$ and set $J\subseteq I$ of indices of the sets containing $v$ (with $w(v,\emptyset)=0$), the weight $w(A_I)$ is the sum over vertices of $w(v,\{i:v\in A_i\})$, and the problem is to optimise $w(A_I)$ over the tuples satisfying $\pi$. For a minimization problem, $\pi$ is monotone if supersets of valid solutions are valid (componentwise), and one minimises the weight. An $r$-shallow minor of $G$ is a graph obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint subgraphs of radius at most $r$; a class has bounded expansion if there is a function $f$ such that for every $r\ge0$ every $r$-shallow minor of a graph in the class has average degree at most $f(r)$. A multiset $\mathcal{Z}$ of vertex subsets of $G$ is an $(s,\delta)$-generic cover if every set of at most $s$ vertices is contained in at least $\delta|\mathcal{Z}|$ members of $\mathcal{Z}$; its treewidth is the maximum treewidth of $G[Z]$, $Z\in\mathcal{Z}$. A class is fractionally treewidth-fragile if there is a function $f$ such that every $G$ in the class has, for all positive integers $s,o$, an $(s,1-1/o)$-generic cover of treewidth at most $f(os)$ (equivalently, in the usual formulation: there is a system of vertex sets, each vertex lying in at most a $1/o$ fraction of them, whose deletion each leaves treewidth at most $f(o)$); it is efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile if such a cover (of polynomial size) can be found in polynomial time. A PTAS is a polynomial-time algorithm achieving approximation ratio $1+\varepsilon$ for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. The author proves, for monotone maximization problems (where subsets of valid solutions are valid) expressible in first-order logic, a linear-time constant-factor approximation in every class of bounded expansion and a PTAS in every efficiently fractionally treewidth-fragile class. The technique applies to minimization problems only with error bounded by a fraction of the total vertex weight rather than of the optimum, so these questions remain open for minimization; as a simplest case, it is unknown whether a PTAS exists for weighted vertex cover in fractionally treewidth-fragile graph classes.

title: Problem 7
statement_text: Do monotone maximization problems expressible in the first order logic admit an $O(n^{o(1)})$-factor approximation for $n$-vertex graphs from nowhere-dense classes?
context_text: For a finite index set $I$, a property $\pi$ of $I$-tuples $A_I=(A_i)_{i\in I}$ of vertex subsets of $G$ is expressible in first-order logic if it is the set of tuples satisfying a fixed first-order sentence using quantification over vertices, the adjacency predicate, equality and unary predicates $X_i$ interpreted as the sets $A_i$. Given a weight assignment $w(v,J)\ge0$ for each vertex $v$ and set $J\subseteq I$ of indices of the sets containing $v$ (with $w(v,\emptyset)=0$), the weight $w(A_I)$ is the sum over vertices of $w(v,\{i:v\in A_i\})$, and the problem is to optimise $w(A_I)$ over the tuples satisfying $\pi$. Here $\pi$ is monotone if every componentwise subset of a tuple satisfying $\pi$ also satisfies $\pi$, and one maximises the weight. An $r$-shallow minor of $G$ is a graph obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint subgraphs of radius at most $r$; a class has bounded expansion if there is a function $f$ such that for every $r\ge0$ every $r$-shallow minor of a graph in the class has average degree at most $f(r)$. A class is nowhere dense if for every $r\ge0$ there is $t$ such that $K_t$ is not an $r$-shallow minor of any graph in the class. The author proves that such problems admit a linear-time constant-factor approximation in every class of bounded expansion. Many results for classes with bounded expansion extend to nowhere-dense classes with constants replaced by $n^{o(1)}$ terms, but the paper's approach does not apply there because it relies on a quantifier elimination result specific to bounded-expansion classes, which leaves the question open.
